chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: His son born in 1937, the death of his first wife in 1946
summary: Jones recalls staying in New York when his son was born on January 4, 1937, and Hinton recalls his wife's death in 1946 and how life shaped the section.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: We got to Joanne. The first baby, a boy, was lost in childbirth. Then there was Joanne and Jonathan, right?

My son was born January the 4th, 1937, and I had a gun in my pocket and I was going to back to Chicago and Gene Krupa, Benny Goodman, Vido Musso, John Alexander, missed breakfast at the Roseland Ballroom, said you can't leave John Hammond. I said, I'm going, my wife's going to have a baby. Mr. Chick Webb said, "Why don't you stay here, son." I said, "Well, I'll stay for another week." So I stayed.
Now we know that as fate has it and the Lord, you lost your beautiful wife - what year did you lose your wife?

In 1946 you lost your wife. I know the story; I know that this is one of the strong things that made that rhythm section so very powerful, how you came to the aid of Walter Page when he had troubles with his family and how that rhythm section rallied around you and how you walked on - I know, Jo, how you walked on that bandstand and how that band played when you heard this very sad news. But this is one of the things that strengthened you and made that rhythm section - and made you strong.

That's .... made the rhythm section. That's what made the rhythm section - living. A man said, 'Experience is based upon mistakes.' Now we don't know - you've got a million mistakes. We don't know what mistakes a human being has made, but when you live with peoples, see the most important thing is the word understanding. The only (sing) 'Say it with music'. We don't know no other way to do it. We don't have stocks and bonds; we don't have the coal, iron, and steel, you see. We can only set it to music. Our feelings when we get to our instrument, we put it out to peoples of the world because we belong to three and a fourth billion peoples. See, we come in the world

with nothing; we go out with nothing, so we're supposed to do these things. What do we care about the materialistic things? Milt, that don't mean nothing to me and you. We don't get a chance to enjoy it anyway. When are we going to swim in that swimming pool?
We enjoy playing, Jo. We enjoy each other.
